This is their second season in a pot and they have been putting up bines for the last few weeks. I was hmming and hawing about where to plant them so they get enough light, and worrying about poor soil and green hugelkultur beds but I went for it anyway.

I had prepared some hugelkultur beds about a week ago. Not elaborate ones, just using twigs, sticks and weeds and some compost but they are quite fresh and this is my first attempt at hugeling. I was worried they wouldn't be rotted enough. Indeed, the grass and weeds were still green despite being buried for a week.

Two of the beds get good exposure, 6 hours of sun or more even now, but the last has a 4 foot wall to clear before it gets sun. There is some reflected light for that bed but we'll see if it's enough. I planted the furthest along hops in the more shaded spot, hopefully the bines are tall enough to see how close the light is.
Finally broke down and put my potted hops in the ground.

No worries man, this hobby is all trial and error. My hugel bed was made from fresh wood and I planted right into it first year, of course I added really rich soil to it, but shit still grew. Best of luck, keep us updated.
